summary: Atsushi Kiyozawa worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Delhi and held a lecturer position at Kindai University (attested 1989).

Atsushi Uno was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti and others. He taught at Shuchiin, Kyoto, and Tokai universities, Hiroshima University (1974–1986), and Kindai University (attested 1988–1989).

Atsuuji Ashikaga studied at Doshisha University and under Ryosaburo Sakaki (~1920–1924). Working in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, he served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1950–1965).
Atsuyoshi Keika is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer (attested 1990) and later as a professor (attested 2014) at Otani University.

August Fick was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (~1852–1856). He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1869–1887) and the University of Breslau (1888–1891).

August Friedrich Pott was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1821–1827) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1830–1833). In 1833, he was appointed Professor of General Linguistics at the University of Halle-Wittenberg.

August Johan Bernet Kempers studied at Leiden University (~1926–1933) and worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as director of the Pusat Penelitian Arkeologi Nasional (~1947–1953) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig, Kiel, and Jena, learning under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He held posts at Jena and Göttingen before serving as a professor at Leipzig University (~1870–1916).

August Schleicher worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under scholars including Heinrich Fleischer, Heinrich Ewald, and Christian Lassen. He taught at the University of Bonn, Charles University, and the University of Jena.

August Wilhelm Schlegel was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1786–1791) and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (1814). He held posts at the University of Jena (~1796–1801) and University of Bonn (1818).

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as director of Aliah University (~1881–1899) and was secretary of the Asiatic Society in 1891.

Awadh Kishore Narain was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and SOAS University of London, later holding academic posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1953–1971) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1971–1990).

Axel Michaels is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Laxmi Nath Srestha. He held academic posts at the University of Bern (~1989–1996) and Heidelberg University (~1996–2018).

B. Alan Wallace, a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, studied at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and with several traditional teachers. He held a post at UC Santa Barbara (~1997–2001) and headed the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies (~2003).
B. N. Mukherjee was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1951–1956) and later held an academic post there from around 1975 to 1997.

B. R. Ambedkar was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Elphinstone College, Columbia University, LSE, University of London, and University of Bonn, and served as professor of economics at Sydenham College (~1918–1920).

Baatr U. Kitinov is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He earned a Ph.D. in World History at Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra worked in Indology and archaeology. He was Government Epigraphist for India (~1945–1953), served in leadership roles at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1953–1965), and became Professor of Ancient Indian Culture and Archaeology at Panjab University (~1965).
Baiei Henmi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1915–1918) and later held a post at Tama Art University.

Baihui Wu was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1951), Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit (~1952), the Institute of Philosophy (~1956), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978).
